Laudo autem vos fratres quod per omnia mei memores estis:
Now I praise you, brothers, because you are mindful of me in everything,
et sicut tradidi vobis, præcepta mea tenetis.
in such a way as to hold to my precepts as I have handed them down to you.
Volo autem vos scire quod omnis viri caput, Christus est:
So I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ.
But the head of woman is man.
Yet truly, the head of Christ is God.
Omnis vir orans, aut prophetans velato capite, deturpat caput suum.
Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered disgraces his head.
Omnis autem mulier orans, aut prophetans non velato capite, deturpat caput suum:
But every woman praying or prophesying with her head not covered disgraces her head.
unum enim est ac si decalvetur.
For it is the same as if her head were shaven.
So if a woman is not veiled, let her hair be cut off.
tondeatur. Si vero turpe est mulieri tonderi,
Truly then, if it is a disgrace for a woman to have her hair cut off,
or to have her head shaven,
then she should cover her head.
Vir quidem non debet velare caput suum:
a man ought not to cover his head,
for he is the image and glory of God.
But woman is the glory of man.
Non enim vir ex muliere est,
For man is not of woman,
Etenim non est creatus vir propter mulierem,
And indeed, man was not created for woman,
but woman was created for man.
Ideo debet mulier potestatem habere supra caput propter angelos.
Therefore, a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the Angels.
Yet truly, man would not exist without woman,
neque mulier sine viro in Domino.
nor would woman exist without man, in the Lord.
For just as woman came into existence from man,
so also does man exist through woman.
But all things are from God.
decet mulierem non velatam orare Deum?
Is it proper for a woman to pray to God unveiled?
Does not even nature herself teach you that,
quod vir quidem si comam nutriat,
indeed, if a man grows his hair long,
it is a disgrace for him?
Yet truly, if a woman grows her hair long,
it is a glory for her,
quoniam capilli pro velamine ei dati sunt.
because her hair has been given to her as a covering.
Si quis autem videtur contentiosus esse:
But if anyone has a mind to be contentious,
nor does the Church of God.
Now I caution you, without praising,
non laudans quod non in melius,
about this: that you assemble together,
and not for better, but for worse.
Primum quidem convenientibus vobis in ecclesiam,
First of all, indeed, I hear that when you assemble together in the church,
And I believe this, in part.
For there must also be heresies,
ut et qui probati sunt, manifesti fiant in vobis.
so that those who have been tested may be made manifest among you.
And so, when you assemble together as one,
jam non est Dominicam cœnam manducare.
it is no longer in order to eat the Lord’s supper.
Unusquisque enim suam cœnam præsumit ad manducandum,
For each one first takes his own supper to eat. And as a result,
Numquid domos non habetis ad manducandum,
et confunditis eos qui non habent?
Or do you have such contempt for the Church of God that you would confound those who do not have such contempt?
What should I say to you?
I am not praising you in this.

For I have received from the Lord what I have also delivered to you:
quoniam Dominus Jesus in qua nocte tradebatur,
on the same night that he was handed over,
which shall be given up for you.
Do this in remembrance of me.”
Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine:
saying: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.
Do this, as often as you drink it,
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup,
you proclaim the death of the Lord,
And so, whoever eats this bread,
or drinks from the cup of the Lord, unworthily,
reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini.
shall be liable of the body and blood of the Lord.
But let a man examine himself, and,
et sic de pane illo edat,
in this way, let him eat from that bread,
Qui enim manducat et bibit indigne,
For whoever eats and drinks unworthily,
eats and drinks a sentence against himself,
not discerning it to be the body of the Lord.
many are weak and sick among you,
But if we ourselves were discerning,
then certainly we would not be judged.
we are being corrected by the Lord,
ut non cum hoc mundo damnemur.
so that we might not be condemned along with this world.
when you assemble together to eat,
so that you may not assemble together unto judgment.
